audit_trail_note: Initial adversarial probes at af38f52a found 1 blocking defect (case-sensitive banned-literal regexes in 1D, 1E, 1G groups). The defect was fixed in commit 0aa410bf during this audit session. The fix moved the finding from blocking_findings to nonblocking_findings as a 'fixed-during-audit' entry. Status 'pass' is appropriate because no outstanding blockers remain at HEAD 0aa410bf.
summary: Phase 1 Website Claims Correction survives adversarial testing with one real bypass defect found and fixed. Initial state at af38f52a had case-sensitive banned-literal regexes in groups 1D, 1E, and 1G — a regression could have re-introduced banned model names (gpt-5, GPT-5), placeholder case studies (school a (coming soon)), or absolute claims (zero risk, aka 2019) in any case variant and bypassed the tests. Fixed in commit 0aa410bf by adding the /i flag to those four regexes. All 20/20 phase-w3-claims tests pass after the fix, lint clean, check-types clean, Wave 2 helper regression check 12/12 green, whole-www suite shows same 11 pre-existing .test.tsx load failures (next-intl/next/navigation resolution) — no new failures introduced. Three additional non-blocking findings (multi-space whitespace bypass in 1A, ASCII '3x' bypass in 1G, multi-line published-case-study helper limitation in 1H/Wave 2) and one coverage gap (banned literals in apps/www-reading-advantage/docs/pr/*.md and apps/www-reading-advantage/measure/*.{md,DESIGN.md,REFACTOR.md}) are documented as known limitations and do not block Phase 1.

nonblocking_findings.title: 1A multi-space whitespace bypass
nonblocking_findings.description: Group 1A's 'nine products' / 'all 9 products' / 'one engine, nine' regex matches literal single-space only. A regression writing 'nine  products' (double space) or 'all  9 products' bypasses the test. Verified: edited home.ts title to 'One engine. Nine  products today' and to 'One engine. All  9 products today' — both passed the 1A test.
nonblocking_findings.recommendation: Optional: normalize whitespace before matching, or use /nine\s+products/ to allow flexible whitespace. Does not block Phase 1 — bypass requires deliberate double-space formatting unusual in normal copy.

nonblocking_findings.title: 1G ASCII '3x' / '3X' variant bypass
nonblocking_findings.description: Group 1G's scoped '3×' regex (CC-25) matches only the Unicode multiplication sign (U+00D7). ASCII variants '3x faster' / '3X faster' / '3 X' are not caught. Verified: edited math-advantage.ts to add '3x faster than traditional math instruction' — passed the 1G test.
nonblocking_findings.recommendation: Optional: extend regex to /3[x×X]\s*/g to cover ASCII variants. Already known limitation NB1 in phase-1-acceptance.json. Low risk — the '3x faster' claim is currently removed (Math page is roadmap-labeled per CC-13).

nonblocking_findings.title: Wave 2 helper multi-line published-case-study bypass
nonblocking_findings.description: The Wave 2 product-claim-helper.ts classify() function processes claims on a per-line basis. Published-case-study detection requires BOTH a school-name hint AND an outcome token on the SAME line. A future real case study that uses the natural TypeScript object structure (school name on one line, outcome metric on the next) would NOT be detected as published-case-study and would bypass the A2 consent gate. Verified: modified case-studies.ts to add school: 'Saraburi Wittaya School' on one line and outcome: 'Reading scores improved 25% across the cohort' on the next — 1H test passes (helper.audit() returns publishedCaseStudyCount=0, missingConsentCount=0).
nonblocking_findings.recommendation: Wave 2 helper improvement — change classify() to operate on multi-line claim blocks (paragraph context) rather than single lines. Or change the Phase 1 1H test to feed the helper multi-line claim blocks (e.g. 5-line windows around school: fields) so it can detect published case studies in structured format. Resolution deferred to Phase 6 closeout when Tier 2 [NEEDS-PO] real case studies are reintroduced. Currently 0 published case studies, so the bypass is theoretical.

nonblocking_findings.title: Coverage gap — banned literals in apps/www-reading-advantage/docs/pr/*.md, measure/DESIGN.md, measure/REFACTOR.md, todo.md
nonblocking_findings.description: Phase 1 source scan is scoped to apps/www-reading-advantage/src/. Banned literals (GPT-5, Google Gemini & GPT-5) exist in: apps/www-reading-advantage/docs/pr/job-posting-lead-generation.md:112, apps/www-reading-advantage/docs/pr/AGENTS.md:131/136/142/236, apps/www-reading-advantage/docs/pr/managed-service-one-pager.md:32, apps/www-reading-advantage/measure/DESIGN.md:230/258, apps/www-reading-advantage/measure/REFACTOR.md:160, apps/www-reading-advantage/todo.md:175. These are PR materials and internal design docs (not the website source). Per phase-0-decisions.md and test-strategy.md §0.B they are explicitly out of Phase 1 scope, but they are arguably public-facing marketing/PR materials that should be aligned with the website claims.
nonblocking_findings.recommendation: Open a follow-up track (Wave 5 / cross-track) to align marketing/PR materials with the corrected website claims. Or extend Phase 1 source scan to include apps/www-reading-advantage/docs/ in a future phase. Not blocking — Phase 1 explicitly targets the website source.
